scope: P-MEM: add self-contained baremetal memory-performance workloads for sequential bandwidth, pointer-chase/random latency, and load/store/pair throughput. No Verilator or Quartus run.

runs.command: for f in baremetal/perf/t_mem_seq.c baremetal/perf/t_mem_random.c baremetal/perf/t_mem_ldst.c; do aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc -O2 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostartfiles -mabi=lp64 -mgeneral-regs-only -Wall -Wextra -c $f -o /tmp/$(basename ${f%.c}).o; done
runs.summary: All three P-MEM sources compile cleanly with the bare-metal cross flags.

runs.command: for f in t_mem_seq t_mem_random t_mem_ldst; do aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc -O2 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostartfiles -mabi=lp64 -mgeneral-regs-only -DPERF_STANDALONE -I baremetal -c baremetal/perf/$f.c -o /tmp/$f.o && aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc -O2 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -mabi=lp64 -c baremetal/startup_mb.s -o /tmp/startup_mb.o && aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc -nostdlib -T baremetal/link.ld -o /tmp/$f.elf /tmp/startup_mb.o /tmp/$f.o && aarch64-linux-gnu-objcopy -O binary /tmp/$f.elf /tmp/$f.bin; done
runs.summary: Each workload links into a standalone bare-metal ELF/bin using PERF_STANDALONE and the existing startup/linker, without changing shared build inputs.

known_limits: perf_common.h is not merged; each file is self-contained as requested.
The three workloads are not wired into scripts/build-microbench.sh, microbench_main.c, or the Makefile; standalone PERF_STANDALONE build/run is provided.
No Verilator microbench_runner execution, no Quartus, and no actual cycle measurements were performed; only compile/link verification.
Fixed scratch addresses assume the 128 MiB physical RAM model (0x40000000..0x48000000).
Performance data is proxy only and is not an A10/Fmax or architectural signoff.
